nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$. The representation $M$ satisfies the Herbrand finiteness hypothesis when its Tate cohomology groups $\hat H^0(G, M)$ and $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$ are both finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness hypothesis for the Herbrand quotient

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring and $M$, $N$ two $R$-linear representations of $G$ whose Tate cohomology groups $\hat H^0(G, M)$, $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$, $\hat H^0(G, N)$ and $\hat H^{-1}(G, N)$ are finite. If there are bijections between the underlying sets of $\hat H^0(G, M)$ and $\hat H^0(G, N)$ and between those of $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$ and $\hat H^{-1}(G, N)$, then the Herbrand quotients of $M$…
nodes.title: Herbrand quotients agree when Tate cohomology in degrees $0$ and $-1$ is in bijection

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$ whose Tate cohomology groups $\hat H^0(G, M)$ and $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$ are finite. Then the number of elements of $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$ is nonzero.
nodes.title: The denominator of the Herbrand quotient is nonzero

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$ whose Tate cohomology groups $\hat H^0(G, M)$ and $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$ are finite. Then the number of elements of $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$ is positive.
nodes.title: The denominator of the Herbrand quotient is positive

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$ whose Tate cohomology groups $\hat H^0(G, M)$ and $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$ are finite. Then the Herbrand quotient of $M$ equals the rational number $|\hat H^0(G, M)| / |\hat H^{-1}(G, M)|$, where $|X|$ is the number of elements of $X$.
nodes.title: Herbrand quotient as a ratio of orders

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$ whose Tate cohomology groups $\hat H^0(G, M)$ and $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$ are finite. Then the Herbrand quotient of $M$ is strictly positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of the Herbrand quotient

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$ whose Tate cohomology groups $\hat H^0(G, M)$ and $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$ are finite. The Herbrand quotient of $M$ is the rational number $h(M) = |\hat H^0(G, M)| / |\hat H^{-1}(G, M)|$, where $|X|$ is the number of elements of $X$.
nodes.title: Herbrand quotient

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a finite cyclic group and $A$ a representation of $G$ over $R$. Then for every integer $n$, the Tate cohomology groups $\hat{H}^n(G, A)$ and $\hat{H}^{n+2}(G, A)$ are isomorphic as $R$-modules.
nodes.title: Periodicity of Tate cohomology for finite cyclic groups

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$ and $n$ an integer such that the Tate cohomology group $\hat H^n(G, M)$ is finite. Then the cardinality of $\hat H^n(G, M)$ equals its number of elements, a natural number viewed as a cardinal number.
nodes.title: Cardinality of finite Tate cohomology as a natural number

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$ and $n$ an integer. This is the cardinality of the Tate cohomology group $\hat H^n(G, M)$, as a cardinal number (possibly infinite).
nodes.title: Cardinality of Tate cohomology

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$. The cardinality of the degree-$0$ Tate homology of $M$ equals the cardinality of the Tate cohomology group $\hat H^{-1}(G, M)$.
nodes.title: Cardinality of Tate homology in degree zero

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $R$ a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-linear representation of $G$. For an integer $n$, the cardinality $h_n(M)$ of the degree-$n$ Tate homology of $M$ is defined as the cardinal number of the Tate cohomology group $\hat H^{-n-1}(G, M)$, following the convention $\hat H_n = \hat H^{-n-1}$.
nodes.title: Cardinality of Tate homology

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
